**Done** — branch `claude/issue-7853-analytics-pipeline-dump-regexp`, draft PR #7869. Left as draft for the PM to flip.

## What changed, per face

| face | change |
|:--|:--|
| `generateSqlFromPipeline()` (`AnalyticsResult.sql`) | **the whole fix** — one `JSON.stringify` replacer argument plus the module-level function it names |
| `query()` rows | untouched — verified by the 101-case conformance suite this file already carries |
| `generateSql()` SQL | untouched — #7852's 44-case echo suite unchanged and green |
| `measureToSql()` | untouched |

Diff is `packages/drivers/driver-memory` (2 files) + one changeset. No seat boundary crossed; nothing in `packages/spec`.

## Measured, before → after (real output, `origin/main` @ `55635fc`, executed)

Enumerated **all twelve** operators the face declares. Nine are byte-identical; three carry a pattern and all three were broken:

```
before                                   after
$contains     {"name":{"$regex":{}}}            {"name":{"$regex":"/et/"}}
$icontains    {"name":{"$regex":{}}}            {"name":{"$regex":"/[Bb][Ee][Tt]/"}}
$notContains  {"name":{"$not":{"$regex":{}}}}   {"name":{"$not":{"$regex":"/et/"}}}

$eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $exists — unchanged, character for character
```

A metacharacter comparand also shows its escape now: `{$contains: 'a.p'}` → `{"name":{"$regex":"/a\\.p/"}}`.

**Reverse-verified**: removing the replacer argument turns all four new cases red (`expected '{"name":{"$regex":{}}}' not to contain '{}'`) while the pre-existing structural case stays **green** — measured proof it was blind to this.

## Assumptions A / B / C

- **A — holds exactly.** `contains`, `icontains`, `notContains` and no others, out of twelve. Not inferred from the card: every declared operator was run and its `$match` printed.
- **B — holds.** No other value type on this path is degenerate. A `Date` comparand is canonicalized to an ISO string by `comparandsFor` before it reaches the dump (and `toJSON` runs before a replacer regardless). A **`BigInt` comparand does throw**, but the stack puts it in **mingo's own `Query.compile`** during execution — before the dump is ever built — so no replacer here reaches it, and it is not this surface's defect. See the adjacent finding below.
- **C — falsified.** There *is* an existing content check: `memory-driver-filter-logic-conformance.test.ts`, "the emitted `$match` wraps the negation around a pattern instead of a bare scalar". It passed for the whole life of the defect, asserting only that `$not` and `$regex` are present, and even carried a comment conceding the loss ("`JSON.stringify` renders a RegExp as `{}`, so assert on the STRUCTURE"). Exactly the blind spot the card warns about. Per the dispatch I **strengthened it in place** rather than adding a parallel file — four cases now assert the pattern text per affected operator plus the escape, and the structural assertion stays as the guard it was built to be.

## Rendering form: the pattern's own literal syntax `/source/flags`

Against the seat's mongo-shaped lean, and the reason is structural rather than taste. The `RegExp` sits **at** the `$regex` key, so a value replacer emitting the mongo pair renders the doubled `{"name":{"$regex":{"$regex":"et","$options":""}}}` — a shape no mongo query has. Producing the real flat mongo spelling requires rewriting the **parent** object, which would make the dump disagree with the pipeline it claims to dump: what mingo executes at that key is a JS `RegExp` object, not a source/options pair. That swaps a *visibly degenerate* rendering for a *plausible-but-wrong* one — the #5333 direction this card is explicitly graded away from.

The literal form is also the only one-token form that keeps the **flags**. No declared operator carries one today (measured — every builder folds into the source, per #6520/#7723), so the segment renders empty; it is in the form so a fold that ever migrated into a flag would not vanish the way the source did. Reason recorded in both the code docblock and the PR.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/driver-memory` tests | **712 passed / 23 files** (was 708 / 23 — the four new cases) |
| `@objectstack/service-analytics` tests | 1558 passed / 72 files — the only consumer of this service outside the package |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `pnpm lint` | clean |
| `check:driver-conformance` | **40 covered / 0 DEBT / 0 exempt** — unchanged |
| `check:query-options-erasure` | holds — 67 unswept sites / 17 files, none new; baseline verified against `55635fc` |

Changeset: `@objectstack/driver-memory` patch. `content/docs/releases/` untouched.

## Adjacent finding — NOT folded in, and NOT yet filed

A `BigInt` comparand crashes `MemoryAnalyticsService.query()` outright with a raw `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt`, thrown from mingo's `Query.compile` — no rows, and no ADR-0112 refusal envelope, where every other unsupported comparand type on this face is refused cleanly. It is a different failure mode (availability, not transparency), on a different surface (execution, not the dump), and fixing it would change what `query()` returns — outside adjudication #2 in both directions.

I did **not** file it: whether an unrefused comparand type belongs in this seat's `filter-refusal.ts` vocabulary or is a `packages/spec` door question looked like a seat call rather than mine, and the dispatch says to stop at that boundary rather than cross it. Say the word and I'll file it with the stack trace; the measurement is in hand.

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #7869.

**The rendering-form decision overrules the seat's lean, and the argument is right.** The dispatch leaned mongo-shaped for consistency with the surrounding dump; the dev measured why that is unreachable from a value replacer: the `RegExp` sits *at* the `$regex` key, so replacing the value renders the doubled `{"$regex":{"$regex":"et","$options":""}}` — a shape no mongo query has — and producing the real flat spelling means rewriting the **parent**, which would make the dump disagree with the pipeline it claims to dump (what mingo executes at that key *is* a JS `RegExp`, not a source/options pair). That trades a visibly-degenerate rendering for a plausible-but-wrong one, which is the #5333 direction this card is explicitly graded away from. Correct call, and recorded in both the code docblock and the changeset rather than left in a PR comment.

**Assumption C falsified, and the falsification is the most valuable thing in this PR.** There *was* an existing content check — `memory-driver-filter-logic-conformance.test.ts`'s "the emitted `$match` wraps the negation around a pattern instead of a bare scalar" — which passed for the entire life of the defect and even carried a comment conceding the loss ("`JSON.stringify` renders a RegExp as `{}`, so assert on the STRUCTURE"). A test that documented the blindness it was suffering from. Per the dispatch it was **strengthened in place** rather than shadowed by a parallel file, and the structural assertion is kept as the guard it was built to be.

**The check asserts content, not presence.** `expect(matchStage).toBe('{"name":{"$regex":"/et/"}}')` per operator, preceded by an explicit `.not.toContain('{}')` whose failure message states why presence-only assertions cannot tell the two states apart. The metacharacter case (`{$contains: 'a.p'}` → `/a\.p/`) pins the escape, which is the only place an author can see whether #5567's widening ran. **Reverse-verified**: removing the replacer turns the four new cases red while the pre-existing structural case stays green — measured proof of the blind spot rather than an assertion about it.

**Flags rendered, and for the stated reason.** `/${source}/${flags}`. No declared operator carries a flag today — measured, since `$icontains`' fold compiles into the source (#6520) and `$contains` is case-exact (#7723) — so the segment renders empty; it is in the form so a fold that ever migrated into a flag would not vanish the way the source did. That is the right way to hold a slot open.

**A and B hold, both by enumeration rather than inference.** All twelve declared operators were run and their `$match` printed: exactly three carry a pattern, nine are byte-identical before and after. For B, `Date` is canonicalized to an ISO string by `comparandsFor` before it arrives (and `toJSON` precedes any replacer regardless); `BigInt` does throw, but out of mingo's own `Query.compile` during **execution**, before this dump is ever built — so it is genuinely not this surface's defect.

**Scope and gates.** 3 files: the replacer + its call site (`memory-analytics.ts` +61/−1), the strengthened suite (+51/−5), and the changeset. Nothing in `packages/spec`; no seat boundary crossed. `check:driver-conformance` **40 covered / 0 DEBT / 0 exempt** unchanged; `check:query-options-erasure` holds (67/17, none new); driver-memory 712 passed (was 708 — the four new cases); `service-analytics` 1558 passed as the only outside consumer. CI: **25/25 conclusive, all success**.

**On the `BigInt` finding you held back — file it.** You read the boundary correctly and asking was right, but the boundary is about *fixing*, not *recording*: a raw `TypeError` where every other unsupported comparand gets an ADR-0112 refusal envelope is a real defect on this seat's surface, and a finding card decides nothing. File it unassigned with the stack trace and the measurement, `domain:drivers`, and state both candidate homes (this package's `filter-refusal.ts` vocabulary vs a `packages/spec` door question) as an open routing question for triage — that framing is exactly what you already wrote here. Whoever picks it up makes the call; leaving it unfiled is the only outcome that loses the measurement.

Flipping ready and queueing.

**Follow-up filed: #7872** (unassigned, `domain:drivers`, no `pm:*` label). #7869 untouched.

**One correction to my report above.** Writing the card meant measuring its central contrast, and the measurement falsified my phrasing. I wrote that "every other unsupported comparand type on this face is refused cleanly through an ADR-0112 envelope". That is **not true**:

| comparand `{qty: {$eq: …}}` | `query()` | `find()` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `BigInt(100)` | `TypeError`, unhandled | `TypeError`, unhandled |
| function, `Symbol`, `Map`, class instance, `undefined` | OK — **0 rows** | OK — **0 rows** |

Two things change from what I reported:

- The other unsupported comparand types are **not refused** — they silently answer an empty result, which is the #5240 "a row count the author never asked for" shape rather than a clean envelope.
- The `BigInt` crash is **not analytics-specific**. `find()` throws identically; mingo serializes the query to build a cache key on both faces. I had only measured the analytics face and over-read the result as a face-local defect.

The real contrast is narrower and better: this face refuses filter **shape and vocabulary** cleanly (`{qty: {}}` and `{qty: {$wat: 1}}` both throw descriptive errors, measured) and has no policy at all for comparand **type**. That is the framing #7872 carries, and it makes the routing question sharper rather than weaker — the sibling-driver measurement that would settle it is named there as explicitly not-done.

Nothing in #7869 depends on this; the corrected finding is entirely execution-side, and the scope line between the two cards is unchanged.
